Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the QuantumCloud Technologies Q2 FY24 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing QuantumCloud Technologies' results for the Q2 FY24. With me on the call are David Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Product Officer; and Chris Lee, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Chen.

David Chen:
Thank you, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. QuantumCloud Technologies delivered another strong Q2, marked by significant growth in our core cloud business and increasing adoption of our innovative AI solutions.

During the quarter, our priorities were focused on six key areas:
1. Expanding our global cloud infrastructure footprint.
2. Driving innovation in serverless computing.
3. Enhancing our cybersecurity offerings.
4. Strengthening our partnerships with leading ISVs.
5. Improving customer satisfaction and retention.
6. Investing in our talent pool and fostering a culture of innovation.

I'm thrilled to highlight our enterprise customer wins and large deal momentum, which really showcase the robustness of our platform in this competitive cloud environment. Enterprise adoption is the foundation of our sustainable growth, and we've seen outstanding progress here, surpassing market averages and even some hyperscalers in critical sectors.

Starting with the top-line figures, we secured 28 deals with Fortune 1000 enterprises in Q2, a 45% increase year-over-year and our best quarter on record for net new logos at this level. Among them, 12 were multi-hundred-million-dollar total contract value commitments, averaging $78 million in annual contract value—a 32% rise from last year's Q2. Our remaining performance obligations from these large deals jumped 62% quarter-over-quarter to $4.2 billion, providing solid multi-year revenue visibility. Net retention for our top 200 enterprise customers reached 128%, fueled by ongoing expansions into AI/ML and data analytics workloads.

These achievements stem from genuine customer successes. For instance, we're proud to welcome GlobalBank, a top-5 U.S. financial services leader, as a key partner. They've committed to a $450 million, five-year TCV migration of their core banking platform from on-premises Oracle databases to our managed DBaaS and Kubernetes-based containers. This includes confidential computing powered by AMD SEV-SNP processors for zero-trust data handling, meeting DORA and FedRAMP High standards. GlobalBank highlighted our 40% TCO advantage over AWS RDS—confirmed by Forrester—as decisive, projecting $120 million in three-year savings from auto-scaling and spot instances.

In healthcare, MediCorp, a major European pharmaceutical company, chose us for a $320 million TCV deal to speed up drug discovery with our AI Foundry. They're deploying 10,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs in our Frankfurt and Paris sovereign clouds to train multimodal LLMs on 50 petabytes of genomic data. We won against Google Cloud's Vertex AI thanks to superior inference latency under 200ms at scale and seamless BioNeMo integration for protein folding. Initial outcomes show a 3x faster training process, right in line with AI advancements in life sciences.

Retail leader ShopWorld renewed and expanded with a $280 million, seven-year deal, pushing their total commitment past $1 billion. They're using our Edge Cloud Network for real-time personalization across 5,000 stores, handling 2 billion daily inference requests on Arm Graviton4 serverless functions. This extends their 2022 Azure migration, where we've cut costs 55% via intelligent rightsizing with ML forecasting.

In manufacturing, AutoForge, a top EV supplier, signed a $210 million TCV for Industry 4.0 IoT analytics on our IoT Core with 5G MEC edge nodes. They're processing 1.5 TB per minute from sensors to refine battery production, cutting defects 28% in pilots. This underscores our hybrid cloud prowess, linking SAP HANA on-prem to S/4HANA Cloud with zero-ETL pipelines.

Common themes across these wins include AI modernization and cost control in a tough economy. Enterprise deal sizes grew 25% YoY, boosted by GenAI demand—Gartner projects $80 billion in cloud AI spending this year, up 84%. Our support for PyTorch, Hugging Face, and Ray has featured in 70% of new large deals.

By region, North America drove 65% of Q2 large deal ACV at $1.8 billion, up 50% YoY, as CISOs favor our NIST 800-207 Zero Trust. EMEA surged 70% to $650 million ACV with GDPR sovereign clouds like MediCorp. APAC grew 95% to $450 million, led by Tokyo/Singapore; AutoForge shows our edge in manufacturing digitization over Alibaba Cloud.

Key strategies include our Unified Control Plane for multi-cloud orchestration via Terraform/Crossplane, now in 40% of large deals. Sustainability with 100% renewable U.S. energy and carbon-aware scheduling cuts emissions 35%. Ecosystem plays with Snowflake data clean rooms and ServiceNow ITOM added 15 upsell deals at $45 million ACV average.

Our Q3 pipeline for $100 million+ ACV deals is $12.5 billion, up 55% YoY, 60% AI/edge weighted. We anticipate 40-45% enterprise net new ARR growth in FY24, beating IDC's 28% cloud forecast. Despite talent and capex challenges, our 135% net retention flywheel targets the $600 billion TAM.

These wins affirm QuantumCloud as the go-to enterprise platform for AI transformation.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong to provide a detailed review of our financial performance.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, David. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q2. Revenue increased by 29% year-over-year to $28.7 billion, driven by strong demand for our cloud services. Our gross margin was 68.2%, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency. Our operating margin was 35.2%.

One key efficiency indicator underpinning this record revenue is our compute and storage capacity utilization rates—these metrics power our hyperscale infrastructure, impacting margins, capital efficiency, and scaling for AI, ML, and generative workloads. We define utilization as the percentage of provisioned capacity actively serving customer workloads, accounting for reliability buffers.

Headline figures: Global compute utilization hit 92.3% in Q2, up 410 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 88.2% and 820 basis points YoY from 84.1%—our highest in three years. This stems from our capacity orchestration engine and GPU cluster ramps. x86 CPU utilization was steady at 91.8%, while Arm-based Graviton4 instances, powering 45% of general-purpose compute, reached 94.7% due to power efficiency and ML framework support like TensorFlow and PyTorch.

For storage, blended utilization was 87.6%, up 320 bps QoQ from 84.4% and 710 bps YoY from 80.5%. This includes 89.2% for object storage (S3-scale with exabytes managed), 85.4% for block storage (high-IOPS for databases), and 82.1% for archival. Gains reflect enterprise data lakes for analytics and RAG pipelines.

Regionally, North America (52% capacity) led with compute at 93.8% and storage at 88.9%, driven by hyperscalers and AI firms like OpenAI in Oregon/Virginia, plus media from Netflix/Disney. EMEA improved sharply to 90.5% compute (up 550 bps) and 86.2% storage, via GDPR sovereign clouds in Frankfurt/Paris and EU Data Act migrations. APAC, our growth hub, hit 91.1% compute with 48% YoY capacity adds in Singapore/Tokyo for Tencent/Alibaba/Samsung; storage at 85.3%, improving with ZRS.

These results come from technical advances. Quantum Orchestrator v3.0, our AI scheduler, rightsizes instances with 95% predictive accuracy, cutting idle capacity 22% QoQ. Spot Instances now at 28% of workloads with 99.99% SLAs, saving customers $1.2B and lifting utilization 5 points. Custom silicon like Graviton5 in 18 AZs offers 30% better perf-per-watt than Intel Xeons; Nitro Enclaves hit 96% in finance/healthcare.

Storage enhancements like S3 Intelligent-Tiering auto-migrate 15% infrequent data to Deep Archive, gaining 400 bps. We added 12 hyperscale data centers, including a 500MW GPU farm in Virginia, expanding compute 28% YoY to 45 zettabytes equivalent and storage to 120 zettabytes, with 7-8% headroom.

This drives margin expansion—every 100 bps lift adds ~$450M to EBITDA. We expect compute to 94-96% by year-end via sovereign AI and Trainium2; storage to 89-91%. $18B capex (60% APAC/edge) counters HBM supply issues. We're winning multi-cloud deals with VMware/Red Hat, up 15% win rates.

Our utilization reflects excellence amid surging demand—we're optimizing at hyperscale speed.

Next, I'd like to introduce Raj Patel, who will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. On the technology front, we made significant progress in several areas. We successfully launched our next-generation QuantumSecure platform, which offers enhanced performance and scalability.

A critical element of our tech advancements is our robust data breach prevention and incident response measures. In the cloud arena—where AWS commands 31% share, Azure 25%, Google Cloud 11% per Synergy—trust is our differentiator. Our SecureCloud suite drove 18% of bookings this quarter, up from 12% last year, supporting 99.999% uptime and 42% win rate in top-10 deals.

Our approach spans prevention, detection, response, and strategy, with metrics proving effectiveness.

Prevention leverages Zero Trust Architecture per NIST 800-207, verifying identities, devices, workloads, data continuously. $450M in FY24 security R&D (40% YoY up, 12% of total) powers NexShield with AI behavioral analytics and FIPS 140-3+ encryption.

Technically: 100% data-at-rest AES-256 with customer KMS keys, PQC pilots (Kyber); TLS 1.3 PFS for transit. IAM mandates MFA for 98% workloads, JIT access cuts standing privileges 75%. eBPF micro-segmentation blocked 2.3M lateral attempts in Q2. DDoS mitigation absorbed 1.2 Tbps attacks (up 50% YoY); SBOM scanning prevents Log4Shell vulns.

Efficacy: 99.97% threat block rate (Deloitte audit). Zero customer breaches in 5 years vs. 20% industry average (IBM); NPS 72 in security.

Regionally: North America (62% revenue) FedRAMP High for federal growth; EMEA (24%) GDPR DPAs/Schrems II for 45% bookings; APAC (14%) IRAP for finance share.

Detection via NexHunt SIEM/ML on 10T daily events integrates EDR/NDR/CDR, false positives 0.5%. Transformers catch zero-days at 94% accuracy; flagged 450K anomalies. MITRE coverage 85%, MTTD 47 seconds vs. 24 hours industry.

Response: GSOC in Ashburn/Dublin/Sydney; MTTR 4.2 min P1, containment <2 hours. SOAR automates 70%; quarterly purple teams. 12 incidents handled (20% YoY down).

Financially, SecureCloud at 85% attach, 25% premium, adds $180M Q3 ARR; 55% hyperscaler win rates.

Ahead: $300M 2025 capex for SEV-SNP/AI defenses; SASE M&A; $102B market by 2027 (IDC). PQC by 2026, UEBA full coverage.

Our measures drive 22% growth, 40% SecureCloud margins—we're trusted stewards.

Now, I'll pass it over to Maria Gonzalez for a product roadmap update.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, Raj. We are excited about the market reception to our new Optimizer suite offering. This product is designed to address the evolving needs of our customers in the enterprise sector.

We've made substantial strides in cost optimization initiatives, delivering over $450 million in year-to-date run-rate savings and boosting adjusted operating margins to 32.4%, up 210 basis points YoY. In cloud competition, this discipline is our edge—shaving 12% off cost of revenues to $2.8 billion while revenue rose 28% to $8.2 billion, under guidance.

Our four pillars: infrastructure efficiency, workload orchestration, procurement leverage, FinOps maturity.

Infrastructure: Rolled out 1.2M Graviton4 ARM instances, 40% better price-perf than x86, cutting CapEx/rack 25% to $135K; PUE 1.12. ForgeTrain chips slash AI energy 35% vs. A100s. EMEA Nordic hydro centers cut costs 18%/watt-hour amid 22% energy spikes.

Workload orchestration: Optimizer auto-scaling up 65% QoQ, dropping idle spend 22% ($180M savings). Predictive Spot 40% burst cost cuts; edge nodes process 60% locally, saving $95M egress, holding APAC margins 29%.

Procurement: Savings Plans at 55% capacity (up from 42%), $320M discounts; AMD/Intel deals 17% per-core savings. Renewables offset 45% carbon, $25M rebates; NA facilities opex down 14%.

FinOps: Dashboard for 85% top customers yields 20-30% savings; internal showback cuts shadow IT 28% ($120M).

Impact: 450 bps gross margin to 68.2%, FCF $1.9B up 35%. Reinvest 60% in R&D like enclaves for sovereign AI.

Positioned for $1.4T cloud market (IDC), 15% TCO lead; flat on-demand pricing, 8% customer credits. Q4 $150M more savings, 34% margins. Diversified footprint mitigates risks.

We're engineering growth through efficiency.

I'll now hand it over to Chris Lee to discuss our marketing initiatives.

Chris Lee:
Thank you, Maria. We have been focused on driving brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly effective in reaching our target audience.

These efforts directly fueled our standout total revenue performance, highlighting the strength of our cloud platform amid AI workloads and multi-cloud demand.

Q2 total revenue reached $28.7 billion, up 24% YoY—our 15th straight quarter of 20%+ growth—and beat guidance of $27.0-28.0 billion by 3% midpoint, 2% high-end. FX-neutral: 25% growth despite macro pressures.

Breakdown: IaaS/PaaS led, IaaS $16.2B +28% on Graviton5 (35% workloads, 40% price-perf gain), instance-hours +15% QoQ. Storage $4.8B +22%, Ultra-Durable (12 nines) drawing NetApp/Dell migrations.

AI/ML $3.1B (11% total, +65% YoY) via SageMaker Ultra with H100/Blackwell/TPUs; hyperscalers scaling petabyte jobs, RPO $12.4B +45%.

Networking/edge $2.4B +18%, for 5G/IoT.

Regions: Americas 52% ($14.9B +26%), CloudLift VMware credits closed 240 $100M+ TCV deals. EMEA $7.9B +21% (+23% FX-neutral), sovereign zones beat Azure. APAC $6.6B +25%, Tokyo/Singapore for e-comm.

Validates Intelligent Cloud Everywhere: renewables cut carbon 28%; Outposts/Snowflake/Databricks $2.1B pipeline. FCF margin 32%, $4.5B capex for capacity.

Raised FY24 to $112.5-114.0B (23-25%), Q4 $29.8-30.5B; 95%+ gross, 125% NRR.

Back to David Chen.

David Chen:
Thank you, Chris. We are confident that our strong financial performance, innovative technology, and talented team will enable us to continue to deliver exceptional value to our customers and shareholders.

Looking forward, macroeconomic factors are top of mind, but our mission-critical workloads, AI focus, and sovereignty position us to outperform. IMF sees 3.0% global GDP; we factor in IT scrutiny, inflation, rates.

Economic slowdown: Gartner 20.8% cloud growth; our IaaS 18-22% FY24 (from 25%), but $150B RPO +28%. FinOps tools uptick hybrid contracts 15%.

Inflation/energy/labor: PUE 1.10, but 200-300 bps H2 margin hit; guide op margins 28-29%. $2.5B diversification, 40% US GPUs, rack util 92%.

Rates/capex: FY24 $28-30B flat, 60% AI (1.5M Trainium3), 18-mo ROI.

Regions: NA 22-25% (AI +55% to $4.2B, CHIPS); EMEA 12-15% (sovereign +30%, FX drag); APAC 25-28% (India/Japan).

Geopol/FX: 70% hedged, $200-300M impact; dual-source HBM.

AI hedge: Inference +80% QoQ, Nexara Guardrails for $10B FY26 ARR; auto OEM 50PB migration, 40% TCO.

FY24 revenue 20-23% ($125-130B), 15-18% EPS; FCF $35-38B, $15B buybacks. Clouds clear H1'25.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez:
Thanks for taking my question. David, great color on the enterprise wins—congrats. Can you talk more about how these large deals, especially in AI, are influencing your raised FY24 guidance and any color on pipeline conversion?

David Chen:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, these wins are a strong validation and directly bolster our outlook. The multi-year TCV from GlobalBank, MediCorp, and others adds significant RPO visibility, with AI components in 70% accelerating consumption. We're seeing faster ramps than anticipated, contributing to our FY24 revenue raise to $112.5-114 billion. Pipeline conversion remains high at 45-50% for Q3 $100M+ deals, as customers prioritize our TCO and integration advantages. We're embedding this conservatism around election pauses but expect continued momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh:
Hi team, thanks. Lisa, on cost optimization, the savings are impressive. What are the biggest drivers for the next quarter, and any risks from supply chain or energy costs?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Priya. The four pillars continue to deliver—custom silicon and edge processing are key, with Graviton rollouts and Optimizer adoption providing $150M incremental Q4 run-rate. Procurement commitments and FinOps maturity round it out. Risks like HBM volatility and energy are real, but our diversified 40/35/25 regional mix, renewables, and US fab shifts keep us insulated, targeting 34% op margins. Happy to dive deeper offline.

David Chen:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are committed to transparency and open communication with our investors.

Emily Carter:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
